territorial_scope.description: Applies to foreign organisations and individuals exporting listed items from outside China, including foreign-made items containing Chinese-origin items, as well as to domestic Chinese exporters.

summary.short: MOFCOM Announcement No. 61 (2025), issued with State Council approval under the Export Control Law and dual-use export regulations, requires export licences for rare-earth-related dual-use items, including foreign-made items with a 0.1% or greater Chinese-origin value share. Parts apply from 9 October 2025 and 1 December 2025.
summary.long: The announcement, issued by the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) with State Council approval under the Export Control Law and the dual-use items export control regulations, sets export controls on rare-earth-related dual-use items for foreign organisations and individuals referred to as foreign specific exporters, and for domestic exporters. Export licences from MOFCOM are required before exporting Annex 1 items that are foreign-made items containing or integrating Chinese-origin Annex 1 Part 1 items at a value share of 0.1% or more, Annex 1 items produced abroad using Chinese rare-earth mining, smelting, magnet or recycling technologies, or Chinese-origin Annex 1 items. Applications for military end users, and for importers and end users on control or watch lists (including subsidiaries at 50% or more ownership), are in principle refused, as are applications for weapons of mass destruction, terrorism or military end uses. Applications for end uses involving 14nm-and-below logic chips, 256-layer-and-above memory chips, related production equipment and materials, or AI research with potential military use are reviewed case by case. Humanitarian emergency exports are exempt from licensing if reported to MOFCOM within 10 working days. Domestic exporters must report final destinations and issue compliance notices, and overseas exporters must pass compliance notices to downstream recipients. Clauses (1) and (2) of point one take effect on 1 December 2025; clause (3) takes effect on publication, 9 October 2025.

notes: Dated 2025-10-09 (dateline and 发文日期). Item 8 sets 2025-12-01 as the start date for items 一(一) and 一(二); item 一(三) applies from publication. The registry status adopted_not_yet_in_force therefore covers only part of the text. Attachment 1 (物项列表.wps, item list) and Attachment 2 (《合规告知书》指引.wps, compliance guidance) are referred to but are not in the fetched text, so the controlled items and the compliance notice content are not reviewed. The 0.1% value ratio in item 1(一) and the control and watch lists (出口管制管控名单, 关注名单) named in item 2 are not defined in the text, and the lists are not included. Item 4 applies case-by-case review to certain chip, memory and AI end uses; item 5 requires an e-mail report within 10 working days after export for humanitarian uses. The text contains no penalty or enforcement provisions. The Chinese text prevails for application documents (item 6). Thresholds and obligations are not coded in this pass.

thresholds.measurement: Value ratio computed per overseas-made Annex 1 Part 2 item; the text states no window, aggregation or measuring body.
thresholds.consequence: Overseas-made Annex 1 Part 2 items at or above the ratio fall within the scope of the dual-use export licence requirement for overseas specified exporters.
thresholds.conditions: Applies where the Annex 1 Part 2 item is manufactured outside China and contains, integrates or is mixed with China-origin Annex 1 Part 1 items; also requires the item to fall under para. 一(一).

enforcement.note: The announcement (Arts. 1-8) sets export licensing requirements, presumptions of refusal, case-by-case review, a humanitarian exemption with a reporting duty, and compliance-notice duties, but states no fines, criminal penalties, licence revocation, clawback, suspension or blocking. It cites the Export Control Law and the Dual-Use Items Export Control Regulations as its legal basis; those texts are not part of the fetched document.
